title: Pedestrian and Vehicle Segregation
summary: Workers on foot can be struck by trucks and other mobile equipment, often when they are in a blind spot. Stay alert, stay visible, and make eye contact with the operator before you cross.
talking_points: OSHA says transportation incidents and workers struck by vehicles or mobile equipment account for the highest number of fatal work injuries.
Stay alert and look out for other workers.
Make eye contact with the operator, flagger, or spotter before you walk in front of or behind a vehicle or mobile equipment.
Do not stand or walk in front of or behind equipment unless the operator signals that it is safe. Avoid the operator's blind spot.
Do not stand in shadows or areas where the driver may not see you.
Obey signs. Do not stray into traffic or truck delivery lanes.
Listen for horns and back-up alarms and pay attention to them.
Wear high-visibility clothing such as vests. Flaggers should check the label for performance class 2 or 3. Other workers should wear class 1, 2, or 3.
site_hazards_to_check: Places where walking routes cross truck and equipment routes
Blind spots behind and beside trucks and mobile equipment
Shadowed areas where drivers may not see workers
Missing or hard-to-see signs marking traffic and truck delivery lanes
High-visibility clothing that is missing or does not have the right class label
discussion_questions: Where do our walking routes cross vehicle routes on this site?
A worker crossing a construction vehicle route was almost hit by a large truck turning a corner because he was in the driver's blind spot. What put him in danger, and what could have prevented it?
What will we do at this worksite today to avoid being backed over or struck by a truck or other large equipment?
